findings.tag: plantwide 'Residue (dry) leaving digestion'; A06/A07 digested-slurry streams
findings.issue: The residue tonnage contradicts itself across areas. A04-A07 give ~400-430 t/h dry residue (1.65-1.8 t/t) and '~140 t/h residue solids per unit'. A08/A09 size on 265 t/h (1.1 t/t), and A20 gives ~290 t/h. The A04-A07 figure was worked out as 640 - 256 + DSP, which never subtracts the ~136 t/h of gibbsite combined water (Al2O3·3H2O) that leaves in solution or as vapour. Thickeners, washers, filter presses, the RSA and the settler feed solids load all depend on this number.
findings.correction: Use one residue basis everywhere: ~265-290 t/h dry (1.10-1.20 t/t Al2O3) at 640 t/h dry bauxite, with design ~290 t/h (equipment margin to ~320 t/h). Per digestion unit this is ~90-100 t/h, not ~140 t/h. Delete '400-430 t/h (1.65-1.8 t/t)' from the A04-A07 plantwide table and from the A06/A07 stream compositions.
findings.evidence: Component balance on 640 t/h dry: Fe2O3 ~20% = 128; TiO2 ~2% = 13; total SiO2 ~3.5% = 22; unextracted Al2O3 (total 46.5% minus 40% available) = 42; non-gibbsite LOI (goethite and kaolinite water) ~4% = 26; other ~6. Inert residue is ~237 t/h. Adding DSP Na2O plus anion (~12), causticisation CaCO3 (~8) and TCA/lime solids and minor gibbsite losses (~5-10) gives ~265-290 t/h. The A01 LOI cross-check (24-26%) agrees: 40% x 54/102 = 21.2% gibbsite water. The world average is ~1.0-1.5 t/t, ~1.2 typical (IAI 2015; Evans 2016), and high-grade gibbsitic ore sits at the low end.

findings.issue: There are two inconsistent spent-liquor systems. A11 collects ALL spent liquor (~3,100-3,400 m3/h) in 11-TK-001, heats it in the PL/spent PHEs to 82-90 degC and sends it to evaporation and digestion. A18 then receives spent liquor 'from A12/A13 at 55-65 degC' (~3,050 m3/h) in its own feed tanks 18-TK-001/002, and splits it 1,700 m3/h to evaporation and 1,350 m3/h to bypass. The same liquor is counted twice, the temperatures disagree by ~25 K, and the regenerative heat A11 recovers (~95-110 MW) has nowhere to go if A18 takes cold liquor. Feeding 82-90 degC liquor to effect 6 of a backward-feed evaporator running at ~60-65 degC would flash it on entry and waste most of that heat.
findings.correction: Fix the routing. Precipitation/classification overflow and filtrates go to 11-TK-001 (55-62 degC), then through the A11 interchangers to ~82-90 degC, then to an A18 evaporator feed/bypass split tank. Do NOT draw cold spent from A12/A13 into A18 as well. Then either (a) change the evaporator to mixed feed (hot spent liquor enters a mid-temperature effect, e.g. effect 3 or 4, at ~85 degC) or (b) take the evaporator feed upstream of A11 and accept that only the bypass stream (~1,350 m3/h) recovers PL heat, recomputing the A11 duty (~45-55 MW, or the PL cannot be cooled to 76-82 degC without a much larger trim cooler). Both drafts need one stated choice.
findings.evidence: Liquor and heat balance: 3,000 m3/h PL x 1.30 t/m3 x 3.25 kJ/kg.K x 26 K = ~92 MW, which needs ~3,200 m3/h of spent liquor on the cold side. A18 shows only 1,350 m3/h bypassing to digestion and a 55-65 degC evaporator feed, which is incompatible with the A11 duty.

findings.issue: The cooling-water system is undersized relative to the loads the other areas declare. A20 sets ~10,000 m3/h circulation and ~100-110 MW rejection, with only 30-40 MW for precipitation interstage cooling. The individual areas declare: A12 interstage 45-70 MW and 5,000-7,000 m3/h; A18 surface condensers 50-60 MW and ~5,000 m3/h; A11 trim coolers 5-25 MW and 500-1,500 m3/h; A19 oxalate coolers 8-14 MW; plus compressor, turbine and generator coolers and calciner FBC trim. That sums to ~120-180 MW and ~12,000-16,000 m3/h.
findings.correction: Size the cooling tower for ~150-180 MW at a 10 K range, i.e. ~13,000-16,000 m3/h circulating (e.g. 6+1 cells instead of 4+1). Raise make-up to ~250-350 m3/h, which moves the fresh-water figure toward ~2.5-3 m3/t. Correct the A20 precipitation interstage duty to 45-70 MW so it matches A12.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic sum of the duties stated in the A11, A12, A18 and A19 drafts. Precipitation exotherm check: ~240 t/h Al2O3 precipitated x ~0.55-0.6 GJ/t heat of crystallisation is ~37-40 MW on its own, before the ~17 K sensible cooling of ~3,000 m3/h liquor plus seed (~55-60 MW) and before the heat lost from 30 uninsulated tanks.

findings.issue: The digestion heat balance leaves out the endothermic heat of gibbsite dissolution. Al(OH)3 + OH- -> Al(OH)4- absorbs roughly 25-30 kJ/mol Al(OH)3, ~0.5-0.6 GJ/t Al2O3 extracted. For 256 t/h extracted that is ~35-40 MW for the plant (~12-14 MW per unit). It shows up as a temperature drop of ~8-10 K across the digester train unless the mixed feed is heated above the holding temperature. The live-steam estimate (~23-28 MW per unit, 0.55-0.7 t/t) appears to cover only sensible heating to 145 degC. A12, by contrast, correctly treats the reverse reaction (precipitation) as exothermic.
findings.correction: Add the dissolution endotherm to the A06 heat balance. Either heat the combined feed to ~150-155 degC so the digester exit is ~143-145 degC, or add live-steam trim at digester 1-2. Raise live steam to ~0.75-0.9 t/t Al2O3 (~180-215 t/h MP steam for the plant, ~60-70 t/h per unit) and carry this into the A20 MP header and boiler sizing (total process steam ~1.85-2.0 t/t). Confirm against a licensed heat and mass balance model.
findings.evidence: Heat of gibbsite precipitation/dissolution in Bayer liquor is ~-25 to -30 kJ/mol Al(OH)3 (Misra & White kinetic work; Wefers & Misra, Alcoa TP-19; Rosenberg & Healy 1996 thermodynamic model). The value should be verified, because web verification was not available in this review. Mass basis: 256 t/h Al2O3 = 5,020 kmol/h Al(OH)3 x ~27 kJ/mol = ~136 GJ/h = ~38 MW.

findings.issue: The DSP alumina loss is misleading and double counted. A05 says each tonne of reactive SiO2 'locks up ~0.85 t Al2O3' and puts the loss at ~11 t/h Al2O3. Kaolinite (Al2O3·2SiO2·2H2O) and sodalite DSP (Na2O·Al2O3·2SiO2 basis) have the same Al:Si ratio of 1:1. The alumina that ends up in DSP is therefore essentially the kaolinite's own alumina, which is already excluded from available alumina. The real penalty of reactive silica is soda loss (~0.6-0.7 t Na2O per t reactive SiO2), plus a small alumina loss only if DSP Al:Si exceeds the kaolinite ratio. Counting 11 t/h as an extra loss against the 256 t/h available extraction distorts the recovery and bauxite-factor reasoning.
findings.correction: Rewrite as: 'Reactive silica is precipitated as DSP, removing ~0.6-0.7 t Na2O per t reactive SiO2 (~37 kg Na2O/t Al2O3 at 2% reactive SiO2). Because kaolinite and DSP have the same Al:Si ratio, the alumina in DSP is the kaolinite's own alumina and is not part of available alumina (the laboratory available-alumina assay is net of DSP). Net alumina loss to DSP relative to available alumina is therefore small.' State explicitly that the 40% available Al2O3 basis is the NET low-temperature extractable figure.
findings.evidence: Stoichiometry: kaolinite Al2Si2O5(OH)4 gives Al2O3:SiO2 = 1:2 molar. Sodalite Na8[Al6Si6O24]X2 also gives Al2O3:SiO2 = 1:2 molar (0.85 t Al2O3 per t SiO2 in both). Standard available alumina / reactive silica assay practice (Authier-Martin et al. 2001, JOM) and Smith 2009 (Hydrometallurgy 98:162-176) both treat reactive silica primarily as a caustic-loss driver.

findings.issue: The dilution and caustic numbers do not close. Digester exit C is 250-265 g/L (A06). Diluting ~2,900 m3/h of it with 550-750 m3/h of W1 overflow at 80-140 g/L (A08) gives a PL C of ~225-240 g/L, but A08, A11 and A12 all state 240-255 g/L. A19 also states the W1 overflow is 130-170 g/L, which contradicts A08's 80-140 g/L. Precipitation yield and A/C targets depend on C.
findings.correction: Adopt one consistent set, for example: digestion liquor C 280-290 g/L; digester exit ~265-270 g/L (after bauxite moisture and direct-steam dilution); W1 overflow ~400-500 m3/h at ~130-160 g/L as Na2CO3; PL ~240-250 g/L. Alternatively keep 550-750 m3/h of W1 overflow and lower the PL design C to ~230-240 g/L, which gives a yield of ~76-79 g/L at dA/C 0.33. Make A08 and A19 state the same W1 overflow concentration.
findings.evidence: Mixing balance: (2,900 x 258 + 650 x 110)/3,550 = ~231 g/L. Caustic conservation from digestion liquor (2,750 m3/h x 280 g/L) to PL (3,100 m3/h) gives ~248 g/L only if dilution volume plus water added is ~350 m3/h.

findings.issue: The grinding slurry volumes are inconsistent. A04 adds 440-470 m3/h of mill liquor plus 160-250 m3/h of dilution liquor (600-720 m3/h total), yet claims a 44-48% solids product at ~830 m3/h. At 640 t/h dry bauxite plus 71 t/h moisture, 44-48% solids allows only ~480-560 m3/h of spent liquor. A06 and A18 carry '~600 m3/h liquor with slurry'. 600-720 m3/h of liquor would give ~40-42% solids and ~920-1,000 m3/h of slurry.
findings.correction: Set the total spent liquor to grinding at ~500-550 m3/h (mill ~380-420 m3/h plus pump-box/spray dilution ~120-150 m3/h), giving ~46% solids, SG ~1.70 and ~820-840 m3/h of slurry. Reduce the digestion liquor via the liquor heaters correspondingly (or raise it) so total digestion liquor stays at ~2,700-2,750 m3/h, and update the A18 interface figure (mill liquor ~520 m3/h, not ~600).
findings.evidence: Liquid mass at 46% solids = 640 x 0.54/0.46 = 751 t/h. Minus 71 t/h moisture = 680 t/h spent liquor / 1.31 t/m3 = ~520 m3/h. Slurry volume = 640/2.8 + 71 + 520 = ~820 m3/h.

findings.issue: The lime figure for TCA filter aid differs threefold. A10 states 0.5-2 kg CaO/t Al2O3 (0.1-0.5 t/h), while A20 allocates ~6 kg CaO/t (~1.45 t/h) to TCA in its 40 kg/t total. The A17 (15-40 kg/t, 30-80 kt/yr) and A20 (40 kg/t, ~89 kt/yr quicklime) totals also differ.
findings.correction: Adopt TCA filter-aid lime of ~2-5 kg CaO/t Al2O3 (~0.5-1.2 t/h CaO) in both A10 and A20, causticisation ~25-30 kg/t (A19: 6-7 t/h CaO), and a plant total of ~30-40 kg CaO/t (~65-90 kt/yr quicklime). Make A17 quote the same figure.
findings.evidence: Internal consistency check. Precoat 0.3-0.8 kg/m2 on ~4,000 m2 of filter area every 4-12 h plus 50-150 mg/L body feed on 3,200 m3/h is ~0.2-0.5 t/h TCA, i.e. ~0.15-0.35 t/h CaO equivalent, which supports A10's lower range. A20's 6 kg/t should then be reduced or justified.

findings.issue: The PL temperature chain is not consistent. A11 takes PL in at 100-106 degC, but A08 settler overflow is 98-104 degC and A10 filtered liquor is 95-102 degC (after a 20-40 min tank and Kelly filters). PL cannot gain temperature through clarification and filtration.
findings.correction: Set the A11 PL inlet to ~95-100 degC (design 98). The A11 PHE outlet then reaches 76-82 degC with a smaller duty (~80-95 MW). Re-check the trim cooler duty for a 72-78 degC fill.
findings.evidence: Heat losses only from blow-off (103-108) through dilution with 95-100 degC W1 overflow, settlers, tank and filters.

findings.issue: The stated residence time ignores the seed slurry volume. Growth slurry flow is the PL (~3,000-3,300 m3/h) plus coarse seed slurry (~1,500-2,200 m3/h) plus fine seed (~150-300 m3/h), about 4,000-4,800 m3/h. Through 22 operating growth tanks of ~4,500 m3 (~99,000 m3) that gives ~21-25 h, not 25-30 h. The total is ~28-32 h, not 32-38 h.
findings.correction: Either state growth residence as ~21-25 h and total as ~28-32 h, or add ~4-6 growth tanks (or enlarge tanks to ~5,500-6,000 m3) to achieve the claimed 25-30 h. Confirm that spent A/C 0.36-0.38 is achievable at the chosen residence time and end temperature with a precipitation model.

findings.tag: plantwide bauxite factor and feed rate
findings.issue: The areas use different bauxite factors and feed rates: A01 2.7 t/t (650 t/h dry, 720 wet in A03); A04/A20 2.65 (640/711); A10 2.5-2.6 (600-630 t/h dry). The Darling Range comparison also varies: 3.2-3.8 (A01), 3-3.5 (A14), 3.5-4+ (A17), 3-4 (A10). Grinding is also inconsistent: A03 crushes to -40 mm with 3 bins (3 lines), while A04 assumes -25 mm with 4 bins (3+1 lines).
findings.correction: Freeze one plant basis: 2.65 t dry bauxite/t SGA (net available Al2O3 40%, ~94-95% overall recovery), 640 t/h dry and 711 t/h wet (10% moisture). Quote Darling Range as roughly 3.5-4 t dry/t, marked 'verify, ore and recovery dependent'. Align the A03 crushed top size and bin count with the A04 mill selection (-25 mm, 3+1 bins, or revise A04).
findings.evidence: Check: 1/(0.40 x 0.945) = 2.65. For comparison, NALCO Damanjodi mines ~6.3 Mt/yr for ~2.1 Mt/yr alumina, ~3.0 t/t as-mined (wet), which is consistent with ~2.65-2.7 dry.

findings.issue: The reference configuration is not representative of low-temperature practice. Slurry heaters with PD feed pumps are mainly high-temperature (boehmitic) practice. Low-temperature gibbsitic refineries typically use 'double-stream' digestion in which only the spent liquor is regeneratively heated in shell-and-tube heaters, while the slurry (after pre-desilication) is heated by direct live-steam injection or mixing, using centrifugal pumps only. This avoids kaolinite/DSP fouling of slurry heater tubes (1-4 week descaling cycles in the draft). The draft flags this as an open question but presents slurry heaters as the base case.
findings.correction: For a representative low-temperature reference plant, make the base case liquor-only regenerative heating (6 flash stages to 6 liquor heaters plus live-steam liquor heaters), with slurry pumped by centrifugal pumps and heated by live-steam injection or by mixing with the superheated liquor in digester 1. Keep slurry heaters and PD pumps as an option. Redo the flash-vapour/heater duty split, because the liquor heaters must then absorb all ~45-48 MW of flash vapour per unit, and the live-steam demand rises.
findings.evidence: Published flowsheets of low-temperature Darling Range-type refineries (e.g. Adamson, Bloore & Carr 1963; Hudson et al., Ullmann's) versus high-temperature tube/slurry-heater plants (QAL, European plants). Heat check: flash vapour available is ~78 t/h per unit (~47 MW), and liquor heating from 95 to 128 degC needs ~28 MW.

findings.issue: The sand design basis does not match either reference ore. 10-15% of residue as sand is high for India East Coast khondalite bauxite (low quartz, typically a few % sand) and far too low for Darling Range ore (~40-50% sand). The design ore is the India East Coast type.
findings.correction: For the India East Coast design ore, set sand at ~3-8% of residue (~10-25 t/h) with a 45 t/h design maximum, and state that Darling Range ore would need a sand circuit roughly 5-10 times larger.
findings.evidence: Ore mineralogy: Darling Range residue is reported as roughly half sand (quartz-rich), while East Coast khondalite bauxite has low total SiO2 (2-5%).

findings.issue: The A11 wording 'Cooling below the dew point of the regenerative exchangers' is technically wrong; this is not a dew point.
findings.correction: Replace with: 'Cooling below the temperature achievable against spent liquor (approach limit of the regenerative PHEs) is done in a cooling-water trim cooler.'
findings.evidence: Terminology; dew point refers to vapour condensation, which does not occur in liquor/liquor exchange.

findings.issue: The draft does not mention the boehmite content of gibbsitic ores (typically ~1-5% in Darling Range and some East Coast ores). At 145 degC this boehmite is largely not extracted, and undissolved boehmite can seed boehmite reversion in the flash train and settlers when the liquor is supersaturated, causing alumina loss. Neither A06 nor A08 mentions it.
findings.correction: Add: 'Boehmite present in gibbsitic ore (~1-5%) is largely unextracted at 145 degC and reports to residue (counted in total but not in available Al2O3). Undissolved boehmite can seed boehmite reversion between digestion and the settlers, so residence time from blow-off to settler overflow is kept short.' Include the boehmite figure in the ore specification.
findings.evidence: Standard low-temperature Bayer practice and known boehmite reversion losses at gibbsitic refineries (Light Metals literature).

findings.issue: The digester design temperature (~175 degC) is lower than the temperature the contents can reach at relief conditions. Digester 1 takes direct MP steam at 10-12 barg (saturation ~184-192 degC) through 06-SI. The 06-HX-301..306 live-steam heaters can also push liquor toward ~185 degC. With a blocked outlet and steam still on, the vessel heats until the PSV lifts at 9 barg plus accumulation. Liquor at ~10-11 bar(a), with BPE of ~6 K, boils at ~186-190 degC. That exceeds the design temperature, which sets the allowable stress (UG-23 / ASME II-D) and the PWHT/SCC envelope.
findings.correction: Set digester design conditions to about 9-10 barg at 200 degC, or at least 195 degC (MDMT to site minimum), and confirm wall thickness at that temperature. SA-516-70 allowable stress is essentially unchanged to about 200 degC, so thickness stays about 24-26 mm including 6 mm CA. Size the PSVs per API 521 for the blocked-outlet case with full steam to 06-SI plus heater steam. Interlock 06-SI and the live-steam heater steam valves on high digester pressure and temperature as a SIL-rated SIS function.
findings.evidence: ASME BPVC VIII-1 UG-20: design temperature must not be less than the mean metal temperature expected at the coincident pressure. The steam saturation temperature at 11 barg is ~187 degC (IAPWS-IF97). The draft gives MP steam at 10-12 barg (A06/A20).

findings.issue: Flash tank 1 has a design pressure of ~6 barg, but the digesters upstream operate at up to 6.5 barg (design 9 barg). If the digester let-down valve fails open or is bypassed, FT1 sees digester pressure plus a two-phase flashing flow. The draft lists a PSV on each flash tank but sets no relief case. Gas/vapour blow-by through a wide-open valve with the digester inventory flashing is normally the governing case, and it is large.
findings.correction: Either (a) rate FT1 for the same design pressure as the digesters (~9-10 barg and FV), or (b) keep 6 barg and size the FT1 PSV per API 520/521 for the 'control valve failed open' two-phase case (DIERS/HEM method), discharging to 06-TK-201. Option (a) is usually cheaper. Also state the hydrotest at 1.3 x MAWP (UG-99) and include PSV inlet/outlet lines and the relief header in the 3-D model.
findings.evidence: API 521 Section 4.4.8 (control valve failure) and 4.4.14 (gas blow-by). Draft values: digester operating 4.5-6.5 barg (A06) vs FT1 design ~6 barg (A07).

findings.issue: Residue tonnage is inconsistent across areas. A06 gives ~140 t/h per unit (400-430 t/h, 1.65-1.8 t/t). A08/A09 give 265 t/h (1.1 t/t). A20 gives 280-300 t/h. The A06 figure does not remove the ~136 t/h of gibbsite combined water that leaves as liquor water: 256 t/h Al2O3 x 54/102. Thickeners, washer pumps, filter presses, the RSA fleet and RSA volume all scale on this number.
findings.correction: Use a single design residue of ~1.15-1.2 t dry residue per t Al2O3, i.e. ~280-290 t/h at 241 t/h Al2O3. Basis: 640 t/h dry bauxite - 256 Al2O3 extracted - ~140 combined water + ~9 Na2O to DSP + ~10-15 lime-derived solids. Size A08-A09 for ~300-320 t/h design (110%). Correct the A06 stream to '~93-97 t/h residue per unit'.
findings.evidence: Stoichiometry of Al2O3.3H2O (156/102). The draft A20 note already identifies this error. World residue average ~1-1.5 t/t (Evans 2016, cited in the A09 draft).

findings.issue: The HRSG steam rating is not achievable with the stated firing. With GT exhaust of 80-100 kg/s and duct firing to ~800-850 degC, a single-pressure HRSG at 64 bar(a)/475 degC with ~140 degC stack temperature can raise only ~85-100 t/h. Example: 90 kg/s x 1.15 kJ/kgK x (850-140) K = ~73 MW, divided by ~2,850 kJ/kg = ~92 t/h. Reaching 150 t/h would need an HRSG inlet of ~1,250-1,300 degC, which requires a fully fired, water-wall furnace HRSG, not duct burners. Installed capacity is therefore about 2 x 95 + 2 x 150 = ~490 t/h. With N+1 (loss of one 150 t/h boiler) only ~340 t/h is available, against a demand of 410-440 t/h.
findings.correction: Rate the HRSGs at ~90-100 t/h each with supplementary firing to ≤850-900 degC. Then (a) add a third auxiliary boiler, or (b) uprate the auxiliary boilers to ~2 x 200 t/h (field-erected), so the N-1 steam capacity is ≥ ~440-460 t/h. Remove the '150 t/h fired' figure.
findings.evidence: HRSG heat balance (cp exhaust ~1.1-1.15 kJ/kgK). Unlined duct burners are typically limited to ~870-950 degC liner/duct temperature (vendor practice for Coen/John Zink duct burners). Steam enthalpy rise feedwater→64 bar/475 degC is ~2,850 kJ/kg (IAPWS-IF97).

findings.issue: The mill feed bins and weigh feeders are specified twice, and the two versions conflict. A03 has 3 bins of 10-12 m dia, 1,200-1,800 t each, -40 mm feed (P80 20-25 mm), 3 grinding lines. A04 has 4 bins (3+1) of 8-9 m, 500-800 t each, -25 mm feed (F80 10-20 mm), 4 mill lines. The modeller cannot build both.
findings.correction: Make A04 own the bins and feeders: 04-BN-001..004 and 04-WF-001..004, 4 bins (3 operating lines + 1 standby), ~700-1,000 t live each, giving ~3-4 h at 237 t/h wet. Delete 03-BN/03-WF and end A03 at shuttle conveyor 03-CV-005 above the bins. Agree one crushed product: -25 mm nominal (P80 ~15-20 mm) for single-stage ball milling, with the secondary sizer gap set accordingly.
findings.evidence: Draft A03 and A04 equipment lists. A04 bases its ball mill and top-ball size on -25 mm feed.

findings.issue: A ball top-up size of 50-75 mm is too small for feed of F80 10-20 mm and top size 25 mm in a 4.3 m mill. Bond's make-up ball formula with Wi ~10 kWh/t, SG ~2.6, 75% Nc, D 4.3 m and F80 15 mm gives ~90 mm. Undersized media leaves coarse feed unbroken and raises scats and circulating load.
findings.correction: Ball top-up 80-90 mm (high-chrome forged/cast), shown in the cutaway as a graded charge of ~90 down to 40 mm. Alternatively, crush finer (F80 ≤ 8-10 mm) to justify 60-75 mm balls. Confirm with Bond Wi test work.

findings.issue: The flowsheet between A07 and A08 is duplicated and contradictory. A07 pumps blow-off slurry with 07-PP-001..006 (3+3 pumps at 950-1,100 m3/h) to the 'dilution tank'. A08 has its own sand cyclone feed pumps 08-PP-001 (2+1 pumps at 1,500-1,800 m3/h, 450-750 kW) drawing from the 'A07 last flash tank', with cyclones ahead of dilution. That is two sets of pumps for one duty, with different destinations.
findings.correction: Keep one pumping step. Recommended: 07-PP-001..006 (one duty plus one standby per blow-off tank, ~1,000-1,100 m3/h, 25-40 m) discharge to the 08-CY sand cyclone clusters. Cyclone overflow then goes to 08-TK-001 (dilution/settler feed). Delete 08-PP-001, or retain it only if the blow-off tanks gravitate to a common A08 cyclone feed tank. The 450-750 kW rating is also oversized: 1,650 m3/h x SG 1.55 x 30 m is ~210 kW hydraulic, ~320 kW shaft.
findings.evidence: Draft A07 stream 'Blow-off slurry to dilution' and A08 stream 'Digested (blow-off) slurry to sand cyclones'. Hydraulic power P = ρgQH.

findings.issue: The filter press cycle of 20-40 min, giving 40-55 t/h dry per press, is optimistic for fine red mud. A complete membrane-press cycle (close, fill, squeeze, cake wash, air blow, open, plate shift and discharge of ~150 plates, cloth wash) on bauxite residue is normally ~60-120 min. Plate shifting and discharge alone take ~10-20 min on 140-160 chambers. One press of 1,000 m2 with 40 mm cake holds ~20 m3 of cake, ~28-30 t dry per cycle, which gives only ~15-28 t/h. Six operating presses would therefore deliver ~90-170 t/h, not 265-300 t/h.
findings.correction: Base the design on a ~60-90 min cycle and ~20-25 t/h dry per 1,000 m2 press (2.0 x 2.0 m or 2.5 x 2.5 m plates). That needs ~12-14 operating presses + 2 standby for ~290 t/h. Alternatively use larger 2.5 x 2.5 m presses with fast-opening group plate shifting: ~10 operating + 2 standby. Resize the press building to ~200-240 m x 35 m, or two buildings, and resize feed pumps, compressed air and conveyors. Confirm with vendor pilot press tests on project residue.
findings.evidence: Cake volume = area/2 x thickness = 1,000/2 x 0.04 = 20 m3. Dry cake bulk density ~1.4-1.5 t/m3 at 72-75% solids, so ~28-30 t per cycle. Industry/vendor practice for bauxite residue presses (Andritz, Diemme, Matec) quotes cycles of ~1-2 h; verify with vendor because live search was not available.

findings.issue: The cooling-water balance does not close. A18 needs ~5,000 m3/h (2 x 25-30 MW). A12 interstage needs 5,000-7,000 m3/h (45-70 MW). The A11 trim coolers need 500-1,500 m3/h (5-25 MW). Oxalate coolers and lube coolers add more. Total is ~11,500-14,500 m3/h and ~125-170 MW. A20 sizes the cooling tower at 10,000 m3/h and ~100-110 MW, and quotes interstage duty as 30-40 MW, which contradicts A12.
findings.correction: Size the cooling tower at ~14,000-15,000 m3/h circulating and ~160-175 MW rejection at 10 K range, as 6-7 cells (N+1) of ~15 x 15 m. Use 4 CW pumps (3+1) of ~4,800-5,000 m3/h each at 35-40 m (~650-700 kW). Use main headers of DN1,400-1,600. Align the A20 interstage duty with A12 (45-70 MW).
findings.evidence: Sum of the draft CW demands in A11, A12, A18 and A19. Q = m x cp x ΔT gives ~4.18 MW per 1,000 m3/h per 10 K → ~14,000 m3/h for ~150 MW.

findings.issue: Shell-and-tube slurry heaters in a low-temperature (gibbsitic) double-stream configuration, fed by PD pumps at 15-22 barg, are presented as the base case. Many gibbsitic refineries heat slurry only by direct steam (or not at all) and heat liquor indirectly, using centrifugal feed pumps. The draft offers this only as an open question, yet the PD-pump justification text says PD pumps are 'widely used where slurry heaters are installed' as if the choice were settled. Diaphragm elastomer limits at ~100 degC caustic must also be confirmed.
findings.correction: Keep the double-stream design as a modelled option. State explicitly that it is a design choice, not standard low-temperature practice, and get SME confirmation before building it in 3-D. If kept: diaphragm elastomer rated ≥110 degC in caustic, propelling oil cooler, dampener pre-charge 60-80% of discharge pressure, and PD pump suction stabiliser.
findings.evidence: Draft A06 open questions. Weir GEHO TZPM literature (verify, no web access in this run).

findings.issue: The P01 cyclone inlet duct of ~2.5 x 4 m is far too large. At ~60 m3/s per cyclone (half of ~120 Am3/s) it gives ~6 m/s inlet velocity. Preheater cyclones are designed for ~15-22 m/s at the inlet, otherwise separation efficiency collapses. The ESP text is also inconsistent: '0.8-1.2 m/s' does not match a ~20 x 13 m flow section, which gives ~0.45 m/s at 120 m3/s.
findings.correction: P01 inlet ~3.0-3.5 m2 each (e.g. ~1.5 x 2.2 m tangential scroll inlet) for ~18-20 m/s. Check P02, P04 and C01-C04 inlets the same way (P04 ~100 m3/s each at ~1,000 degC: ~5-6 m2 inlet). ESP gas velocity ~0.8-1.0 m/s implies ~120-150 m2 flow area. Either state 2 parallel casings or reduce the casing section, keeping SCA ~80-110 s/m.
findings.evidence: Suspension preheater design practice (Duda, Cement Data Book: inlet velocity 15-20 m/s). Draft gas flows ~115-135 Am3/s.

findings.issue: With 2 x 3,500 t/d calciners, a single-calciner outage (refractory, ~2-3 weeks/yr each; trips) leaves ~2,500-3,000 t/d of hydrate with no destination. Precipitation cannot be turned down quickly. The only buffer defined is the 150-300 t calciner feed bin, about 1 h. A15 itself raises this as an open question, but no equipment exists.
findings.correction: Add 14-TK-0xx product hydrate slurry storage tanks: 2 agitated tanks of ~8,000-10,000 m3 holding hydrate at ~50% solids in spent liquor, giving ~3-5 days at one-calciner rate. Feed them from the primary cyclone underflow, with reclaim pumps back to the product filters. Alternatively, provide a covered wet-hydrate storage shed with reclaimer.
findings.evidence: Draft A15 open question (2 x 3,500 t/d calciners). Common Bayer practice of hydrate storage tanks ahead of calcination.

findings.issue: The A11 materials text says carbon steel PL piping is suitable 'below the NACE SP0403 PWHT line'. At 100-106 degC and ~15% NaOH-equivalent, PL service lies above the line on the NACE caustic chart. Welds therefore need PWHT, or the area needs an owner-approved alternative. The same applies to A10 and A08 hot liquor tanks and piping.
findings.correction: State that all carbon steel welds in liquor at >~75-80 degC with C ≥ ~200 g/L as Na2CO3 are PWHT'd: pipe spools, nozzles, attachments and tank nozzle/attachment welds (A04-A11, A18). The A11 PL piping and A10 tanks are included. Spent liquor at <62 degC is not.
findings.evidence: NACE SP0403-2015 caustic soda service chart (PWHT region begins at ~60-80 degC for 10-20% NaOH).

findings.issue: The bottom strake thickness of 28-32 mm is overstated. API 650 one-foot method for D=14 m, H=31 m, G=1.55 and Sd=160 MPa (A516-70) gives ~20.4 mm + 3 mm CA = ~24 mm. The hydrotest case needs ~12.5 mm. Separately, the wide-gap PHE slurry velocity of 0.3-0.6 m/s is low for 600-700 g/L hydrate with particles up to ~150 µm. It risks settling and plugging in the port and distribution zones.
findings.correction: Bottom strake ~24-26 mm, tapering to ~10 mm (minimum per API 650 for D 15 m is 6 mm, plus CA). Interstage wide-gap PHE slurry-channel velocity ~0.8-1.2 m/s, with a low-flow trip and automatic liquor flush.

findings.issue: '~7-8% of the liquor flashes to steam' on a leak at 145 degC is overstated. The flash fraction is cp x ΔT / hfg = 3.2 x (145-107) / 2,240 = ~5.4%. The hazard conclusion is unchanged, but trainees will quote the number.
findings.correction: About 5-6% of the liquor mass flashes to steam on release at 145 degC (more at 150 degC).
findings.evidence: Energy balance with cp ~3.2 kJ/kgK, atmospheric boiling point ~107 degC, hfg ~2,240 kJ/kg.

findings.issue: An outreach of 22-30 m from the fender line is marginal for the stated Panamax design vessel (beam 32.3 m). Fender standoff is ~2-3 m, and the chute must reach about 2-3 m inside the far hatch coaming to trim.
findings.correction: Maximum outreach ~31-33 m from the fender line (shuttle extended), minimum ~10 m, with a shuttle stroke of ~12-15 m.
findings.evidence: Panamax beam 32.3 m. Shiploader practice per AS 4324.1 / FEM 2.131.

findings.issue: Each author uses a different bauxite factor and dry bauxite rate: A01/A03 2.7 (650 t/h dry, 5.4 Mt/yr); A04-A07 and A20 2.65 (640 t/h); A08-A10 2.5-2.6 (600-630 t/h). Equipment counts and sizes (mills, thickeners, pumps, stockyard) are built on mismatched feeds.
findings.correction: Fix a single design value: 2.65 t dry bauxite/t Al2O3, i.e. 640 t/h dry and ~711 t/h wet at 10% moisture, with a 110% design margin (~705 t/h dry). Re-issue the A01-A03 and A08-A10 stream tables on this basis. The change from the provisional 2.4-2.6 should be stated once, in the plant-wide numbers.
findings.evidence: Draft plant-wide numbers in each domain section; 1/(0.40 x 0.95) = 2.63.

findings.issue: The mining method follows Darling Range practice: thin ore, a blasted caprock, and friable bauxite that is free-dug. The design ore, however, is India East Coast khondalite-plateau bauxite. That ore lies under 1-5 m of laterite cap, is about 10-30 m thick, and is compact to hard. At East Coast operations (Panchpatmali, Baphlimali/Utkal, Lanjigarh supply) the bauxite itself is normally drill-and-blast or surface-miner ore, not free-dig. Two operating 89-127 mm rigs drilling only 1-4 m caprock benches cannot break about 3 Mbcm/yr of ore plus cap.
findings.correction: Pick one deposit model and size the fleet to it. For the East Coast design ore: 'Laterite cap 1-5 m (drill & blast or rip, waste or low-grade ore); bauxite 10-30 m mined on 5-8 m benches by drill & blast (115-165 mm DTH, pattern ~3.5x4 to 4.5x5 m, powder factor ~0.25-0.45 kg/bcm) or by surface miners (Wirtgen 2200/2500SM class) as a selective alternative.' Blast-hole fleet: 3-4 operating + 1 standby (engineering estimate: about 3 Mbcm/yr at ~10-15 bcm per drilled metre gives ~200-300 km/yr drilled). Keep the free-dig description only as a note on Darling Range practice.
findings.evidence: Mass balance: 6.3 Mt/yr / ~2.1 t/m3 in situ = ~3.0 Mbcm/yr of ore. The draft itself states East Coast pits are 10-30 m deep, which conflicts with '1-4 m caprock benches'. East Coast operations are publicly described as drill-and-blast or surface-miner bauxite mining (NALCO and Utkal operation descriptions). Live web verification was blocked (WebSearch HTTP 403, nalcoindia.com robots-disallowed), so this is reasoning from published practice and should be verified.

findings.issue: The disturbance rate of 60-110 ha/yr is inconsistent in two ways. It does not match the draft's own basis: 4-8 m ore at 2.0-2.2 t/m3 gives 80-176 kt/ha, not 60-130. It also does not match the East Coast ore that was selected, which at 10-30 m thickness gives about 200-600 kt/ha. The rehab programme, topsoil volume and the clearing scenes in the 3-D terrain sequence are all overstated by roughly 2-4x for the design ore.
findings.correction: Area mined ≈ 6.3 Mt/yr ÷ (ore thickness x in-situ density x ~0.7-0.8 ore-to-pit-area recovery). For East Coast 10-20 m ore: ~20-45 ha/yr (engineering estimate). Keep 60-110 ha/yr only for a Darling Range-style alternative (4-6 m ore, which is consistent with Alcoa practice). Recalculate topsoil from area x 0.1-0.3 m; the current 80,000-200,000 m3 does not equal 60-110 ha x 0.1-0.3 m = 60,000-330,000 m3 either.
findings.evidence: Arithmetic: 1 ha x 4 m x 2.0 t/m3 = 80 kt and 1 ha x 8 m x 2.2 t/m3 = 176 kt. The draft states East Coast depths of 10-30 m.

findings.issue: Dilution is counted twice. The mine sends 6.2-6.4 Mt/yr wet ROM, which includes 3-5% dilution, and there is no rejection step, so all of it goes to the refinery. A03 and A04 then consume only about 5.9-6.0 Mt/yr wet (711-720 t/h x 8,300 h). Unless a beneficiation or reject stream exists, the tonnage mined must equal the refinery feed plus stock change. Dilution lowers the delivered grade and therefore enters the bauxite factor; it does not add extra tonnes that disappear.
findings.correction: Set ROM delivered to the refinery = refinery feed ≈ 5.4 Mt/yr dry ≈ 6.0 Mt/yr wet at 10% moisture, with the bauxite factor (2.65-2.7) applied to the diluted delivered grade. Mine planning carries ore loss and dilution as an in-situ to ROM adjustment only. If a scalping or reject stream is intended (for example hard caprock rejected at the sizer), add it as an explicit stream with tonnage.
findings.evidence: A03 stream: 720 t/h wet x 8,300 h = 5.98 Mt. A04: 711 t/h x 8,300 h = 5.90 Mt. A01: 6.2-6.4 Mt. No reject stream exists other than A04 scats at 0.5-2 t/h (about 4-17 kt/yr).

findings.issue: The claim that the conveyor is 'regenerative on downhill sections' and returns 0.5-1.5 MW to the grid is misleading. A net fall of 150 m over 20 km is only about 0.75% average grade. The draft's own friction figures (about 1.3-1.8 MW per 10 km flight) exceed the total gravity power of the load (500 kg/s x 9.81 x 150 m ≈ 0.74 MW for the whole 20 km). Each flight therefore motors at every load case. Regeneration can occur only on local steep descending sections, transiently, or with uneven loading.
findings.correction: Reword: 'Net motoring overland (average decline ~0.75%); absorbed power ~0.9-1.4 MW per 10 km flight at design load after the gravity credit (~0.37 MW per flight). AFE VFDs are still specified for torque control and to absorb regenerative power on local steep downhill sections and partly loaded or downhill-only-loaded cases, and controlled brakes are required for those sections. The dynamic analysis must check loaded-downhill/empty-uphill cases.' Delete 'Regenerated electrical power ... up to ~0.5-1.5 MW' as a steady-state stream, or show it only as a transient. Regeneration becomes a steady-state design case only if the route slope exceeds about f x m_moving / m_load ≈ 0.014 x 220/111 ≈ 2.8%.
findings.evidence: ISO 5048 / DIN 22101 resistance: P ≈ f·L·g·m'·v = 0.014 x 10,000 x 9.81 x 220 x 4.5 ≈ 1.36 MW per flight. Gravity term per flight = 500 kg/s x 9.81 x 75 m ≈ 0.37 MW. The draft's own figure is 0.7 MW for the total fall.

findings.issue: The A03/A04 interface is inconsistent, and the same equipment is tagged twice. A03 crushes to -40 mm (P80 20-25 mm) and builds 3 mill-feed bins of 1,200-1,800 t each for 3 grinding lines. A04 assumes -25 mm feed (F80 10-20 mm in its Bond calculation) and 4 bins of 500-800 t for 3+1 mills. A03 also places the shuttle gallery at +30-40 m, while A04 places it at +25 m.
findings.correction: Assign the mill feed bins and weigh feeders to one area only (recommended: A04, tags 04-BN/04-WF) and delete 03-BN/03-WF. Fix the number of lines (4 bins for 3 operating + 1 standby mill, each ~600-900 t live, about 2.5-4 h per line). Make the secondary sizer product match the mill design: either -40 mm top size with F80 ~20-25 mm used in the A04 Bond calculation (mill power rises by roughly 10-20%), or a tertiary or closer-set sizer to reach -25 mm. Use one shuttle elevation.
findings.evidence: Comparison of the A03 and A04 drafts. Bond energy scales with (1/√P80 − 1/√F80), so F80 15 mm against 22 mm changes the specific energy noticeably.

findings.issue: The strategic backup reclaim route is undersized. One ~50-t class wheel loader (CAT 980/988 class, about 10-12 t per pass) cannot sustain 900 t/h of load-and-carry into a ground hopper; a realistic rate is about 350-550 t/h. With a single stacker, a single bridge reclaimer and a single reclaim line, the refinery would be starved (it needs about 720 t/h average) whenever the reclaimer is down.
findings.correction: Specify 2 x 988-class loaders (1 duty + 1 standby, combined ≥ 800 t/h) or 1 x 992/994-class loader with a 988 backup. Alternatively add a dozer-trap or reclaim-tunnel feeder under part of the emergency stockpile. State the emergency reclaim rate as ≥ 750-800 t/h wet so it covers mill demand.
findings.evidence: 988K rated payload ~11.3 t. At a 40-60 s cycle with short carry that gives ~700-1,000 t/h peak and ~400-550 t/h sustained at 60-70% efficiency (Caterpillar Performance Handbook class data; engineering estimate).

findings.issue: The emergency stockpile (250-350 kt, footprint ~250 x 120 m, 15-18 m high) is said to be built by 'stacker overflow/bypass' from a rail side-stacker whose boom reaches only about 25-35 m from its rail. The stacker cannot build a pile 120 m wide. Dozing 250-350 kt laterally from a bypass chute means heavy double handling, compaction and fines.
findings.correction: Add an emergency stockpile feed conveyor with a fixed or radial luffing stacker (tag 03-CV-006/03-RS-001), or a slewing stacker that can reach the emergency pile, and state the dozer-push distance. For a 3-D model, show a separate conical or kidney pile fed by a radial stacker.
findings.evidence: Geometry stated in the A03 draft (boom 28-35 m; emergency pile 120 m wide).

findings.issue: The bucket wheel is oversized for 1,000-1,100 t/h. A wheel of 6-7 m diameter with 10-12 buckets of 1.0-1.5 m3 would have a theoretical output of about 3,000-4,000 t/h at normal wheel speeds.
findings.correction: For 1,000-1,100 t/h blending-bed duty use a wheel of ~4-5 m diameter with 8-12 buckets of ~0.4-0.6 m3 (or a 3-4 m drum), and wheel drive ~110-160 kW (engineering estimate). Machine mass ~300-450 t.
findings.evidence: Q = n_buckets x discharges per min x V x fill x ρ: about 12 x 5 rpm x 1.2 m3 x 0.7 x 1.35 x 60 ≈ 4,100 t/h.

findings.issue: The primary cross-belt sampler sits on -200 mm reclaimed ore. Under ISO 8685 the cutter aperture must be at least 3x the top size (≥ 600 mm), which is impractical for a hammer sampler on a 1,200 mm belt. The draft acknowledges this but keeps the sampler before the sizers in the process description.
findings.correction: Move the metallurgical-accounting sampler to after secondary sizing (on 03-CV-004, -40 mm, cutter aperture ≥ ~120-150 mm). Keep the PGNAA plus belt scale on incoming ore for stacking control.
findings.evidence: ISO 8685 cutter-opening rule (≥ 3 x nominal top size), as quoted in the draft.

findings.issue: The haulage and crushing hours do not match. The truck fleet is sized on ~6,000 effective h/yr per truck, which implies near-continuous mining at about 1,050 t/h. The sizer, overland and stockyard are sized for only 4,300-4,900 effective h/yr at 1,300-1,500 t/h. With 60-80% direct tipping, the ROM pad and loader rehandle must absorb the difference, and the 6,000 h figure is optimistic (typical ~5,000-5,500 h after availability, utilisation and efficiency).
findings.correction: State a mine roster (for example 2 x 12 h, 7 d/wk) and use consistent hours: trucks ~5,000-5,500 operating h/yr giving ~0.85-0.95 Mt/yr per truck, so ~7-8 on ore + 2-3 on waste, totalling 10-11 operating + 2 spare. Sizer and overland effective ~5,000-5,500 h at ~1,150-1,250 t/h nominal, with the 1,800 t/h design kept as surge capacity.
findings.evidence: Draft fleet calculation: 165 t/h x 6,000 h = 0.99 Mt per truck. 6.3 Mt / 6,000 h = 1,050 t/h, which does not equal 1,300-1,500 t/h over 4,300-4,900 h.

findings.issue: Waste tonnage does not equal the stated strip ratio: 0.3-0.6 t/t x 6.2-6.4 Mt gives 1.9-3.8 Mt/yr, not 1.5-3.5.
findings.correction: '~1.9-3.8 Mt/yr (strip ratio ~0.3-0.6 t/t)'. For East Coast ore with 1-5 m cap over 10-20 m ore, a ratio of ~0.1-0.4 (~0.6-2.5 Mt/yr) is more representative (engineering estimate).
findings.evidence: Arithmetic.

findings.issue: Mine diesel use of 15-30 ML/yr is high for the listed fleet.
findings.correction: ~10-15 ML/yr (engineering estimate: 11 x 777-class at ~70-90 L/h x ~5,500 h ≈ 4.5-5.5 ML; 3 x 200-t excavators ~150-180 L/h x 5,000 h ≈ 2.5 ML; dozers, loaders, drills, graders, water carts and light vehicles ~3-5 ML). Size the fuel farm at ≥ 7-10 days, i.e. 2-3 x 150 kL.
findings.evidence: OEM fuel-burn class data (Caterpillar Performance Handbook, medium load factor); engineering estimate.

findings.issue: The tyre size is wrong for the named class. A CAT 992-class loader uses 50/65-51 tyres (about 3.4 m diameter); 45/65R45 belongs to the 990 / Komatsu WA900 class.
findings.correction: 'Tyres 50/65R51 (992 class, ~3.4 m dia) or 45/65R45 (WA900/990 class, ~3.0 m)'. Model the tyre to the chosen machine.
findings.evidence: Caterpillar 992K and Komatsu WA900 specification sheets (class data, from memory; verify).

findings.issue: A ~100 t low loader cannot move the 190-210 t excavators. The draft implies it relocates excavators between pits.
findings.correction: State that 200-t excavators track (walk) between pits on haul roads (~2-3 km/h) or are part-dismantled for long moves. The ~100-120 t float is for D10-class dozers and drills only.
findings.evidence: PC2000 / R9200 operating mass ~200 t (OEM class).

findings.issue: The 1,400 mm belts for 2,000 t/h rated and 2,200 t/h design SGA at ~4 m/s are near full cross-section. SGA loose density is ~0.95-1.0 t/m3 and the surcharge angle is low (5-10°, fluidisable), so the fill is about 75-90% of the 35°/10° area. That invites flooding and spillage over water on the jetty.
findings.correction: Use a 1,600 mm belt at ~4.0 m/s (fill ~55-65%), or 1,400 mm at ≥ 4.8-5.0 m/s with a 45° trough. Fit spill trays or a fully enclosed gallery floor under the jetty conveyor (no spillage to sea).
findings.evidence: CEMA/DIN area for 1,400 mm, 35° trough, 10° surcharge ≈ 0.19 m2. Required area = 2,200 / (0.95 x 3,600 x 4.0) ≈ 0.16 m2.

findings.issue: The refinery-to-port mode is undecided and the areas contradict each other. A16 and A17 design an ~8 km covered overland conveyor with a caustic pipeline in the same corridor; A20 assumes 30-60 km by rail (Worsley-Bunbury style). These give entirely different 3-D models (rail loadout and unloader, wagons and loco shed against a conveyor corridor) and different caustic, lime and fuel logistics.
findings.correction: Fix one basis for the generic plant. Recommended: coastal or near-coastal refinery, ≤ 10-15 km, covered overland conveyor at ~800 t/h plus caustic and fuel pipelines. Note rail (covered pressure-discharge or hopper wagons, rail loadout silo and port bottom-dump or pneumatic unloading) as the inland alternative. Remove the 30-60 km rail statement from A20, or add the rail equipment to A16/A17.
findings.evidence: Draft A16 (8 km conveyor) versus A20 plantwide 'Site layout - approximate distances'. Wikipedia 'Worsley Alumina' (fetched): ~50 km mine conveyor; alumina transported 55 km to Bunbury.

findings.issue: Caustic logistics conflict. A17 sends 50% NaOH from 2 x 15,000 m3 port tanks to the refinery by an ~8 km pipeline. A19 receives it by rail or road tankers into 2 x 6,000 m3 refinery tanks with unloading bays. A17 also says lime import is 30-80 kt/yr CaO, while A20 says ~89 kt/yr quicklime.
findings.correction: Pipeline basis: delete the 19-UL-401 rail/road bays (keep one emergency road-tanker bay) and size the refinery caustic tanks at ~7-10 days (~2 x 3,000-4,000 m3), with port storage of 2 x 15,000 m3 at ~2 parcels. Use one lime number: ~89 kt/yr quicklime (~40 kg CaO/t Al2O3 at ~90% available CaO).
findings.evidence: Cross-area comparison of the A17, A19 and A20 drafts.

findings.issue: Dredged depth may be shallow for fully laden Panamax alumina cargoes. Dense SGA cargoes load ships to their marks, at a Panamax summer draft of ~13.8-14.5 m.
findings.correction: 'Dredged berth pocket ~-15.5 to -16 m CD for laden Panamax (draft ≤14.5 m + UKC ~10%), or ~-13.5 to -14 m CD if the design vessel is limited to Supramax (draft ~12.5-13 m)'. Tie this to the open question on vessel mix.
findings.evidence: PIANC UKC guidance (~10% of draft for sheltered berths); typical Panamax summer draft. Engineering estimate.

findings.issue: Arm size and flow are inconsistent. A DN200-250 arm at 1,000 m3/h gives ~5.7-8.8 m/s, too high for 50% NaOH (SG 1.52) and HFO.
findings.correction: 'DN250-300 (10-12 in) arms for ship discharge ~400-800 m3/h (velocity ≤ ~3-4 m/s)'.
findings.evidence: Hydraulic arithmetic: Q / (π/4 · D²).

findings.issue: The Worsley reference flagged as 'verify' can now be partly confirmed. The draft also misses the closest analogues for a generic 20 km plateau-to-refinery overland: Alcoa's Darling Range overlands (Huntly to Pinjarra, Willowdale to Wagerup, ~20-25 km).
findings.correction: Cite: 'Worsley: ~50 km overland conveyor from the Boddington-area (Marradong) mine to the refinery (Wikipedia, Worsley Alumina)'. Add Alcoa Huntly-Pinjarra and Willowdale-Wagerup overlands as references (lengths to verify).
findings.evidence: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worsley_Alumina (fetched this session: ~50 km conveyor, 55 km to Bunbury).

findings.issue: Mercury is missing as a hazard everywhere. Gibbsitic bauxite (Darling Range in particular) carries trace mercury (about 0.1-0.5 ppm). At low-temperature digestion it volatilises and collects in digestion and flash vapour, heater shells, NCG vents, condensate pots and evaporator condensate. It is also emitted from calciner and liquor-burner stacks. The draft never mentions it, so a trainee would open heater channels, condensate pots, NCG lines and vent condensers without Hg controls.
findings.correction: Add a plant-wide hazard: 'Elemental mercury vapour and liquid Hg droplets can collect in digestion/flash heater shells, condensate pots, NCG headers, vent condensers and evaporator condensate. Before line-breaking or entry in these systems: check for Hg (direct-reading Hg vapour analyser), wear respiratory protection with Hg cartridges or supplied air, collect any Hg droplets in sealed containers, and run biological monitoring (urine Hg) for maintenance crews.' Add an Hg removal/condensation step (for example chilled condensation or a sulfur-impregnated carbon bed on the NCG/vent stream) and Hg monitoring on the calciner and LBF stack CEMS.
findings.evidence: Domain knowledge: Western Australian refinery licences (DWER) and Alcoa Wagerup/Pinjarra/Kwinana environmental reports identify mercury in digestion vent and condensate systems and in calciner/LBF emissions. Several WA refineries have fitted mercury condensers on digestion vents. Web verification was blocked in this run, so the SME should confirm the exact references.

findings.issue: The residue rate is given three different ways. A06/A07 say about 140 t/h per unit (about 420 t/h, 1.65-1.8 t/t). A08/A09 say 265 t/h (1.1 t/t). A20 says about 290 t/h. The A06/A07 figure leaves in the gibbsite water of hydration (about 135 t/h at 256 t/h Al2O3 extracted). Thickeners, filter presses, RSA volume and operator mass-balance training all depend on this number.
findings.correction: Use one design value: about 1.1-1.25 t dry residue per t Al2O3, about 270-300 t/h (design 290 t/h incl. DSP and lime-derived solids). Revise A06 to 'residue solids about 90-100 t/h per unit' and A07 to match.
findings.evidence: 640 t/h dry bauxite - 256 t/h Al2O3 extracted - 256 x 54/102 = 135 t/h combined water + about 9 t/h Na2O as DSP + about 10-15 t/h lime solids = about 270-290 t/h. World average about 1.0-1.5 t/t (IAI 2015, Evans 2016).

findings.issue: The descaling hazards contain a placeholder ('acid cleaning gives off H2S? (not expected) but CO2'). They also say hydrogen forms only if the acid touches aluminium or zinc. Inhibited H2SO4 on carbon-steel tubes, tube sheets and shells also gives off H2, especially when the inhibitor is depleted. A06-SK-001 says this correctly, so the two areas contradict each other.
findings.correction: Replace with: 'Acid cleaning of carbon-steel evaporator tubes releases hydrogen (and CO2 from carbonate scale). Ventilate the vessel, keep ignition sources out, monitor LEL continuously during and after the clean, and vent the circuit to a safe location. H2S is not expected unless sulfide scale is present. Contact with zinc, galvanised steel or aluminium makes the H2 release much faster.'
findings.evidence: Acid corrosion chemistry: Fe + H2SO4 -> FeSO4 + H2. A06 06-SK-001 hazards in the same draft.

findings.issue: The confined-space gas-test guidance is incomplete and in one place misleading. A12 says 'continuous gas test (generally O2 only)'. Caustic and residual liquor react with aluminium and zinc (galvanised scaffold, ladders, tool bodies) to make hydrogen. Acid cleaning makes H2. Digestion, evaporator and precipitator vapour spaces can hold VOCs and Hg. Only A18 warns against aluminium tools, and nobody mentions galvanised scaffolding.
findings.correction: For all Bayer vessel entries, the minimum gas test is O2, LEL (H2), CO and toxics (VOC/Hg where relevant). State: 'No aluminium or galvanised scaffolding, ladders or tools inside caustic-wetted vessels. Use painted or bare steel or FRP scaffold.' Remove 'generally O2 only'.
findings.evidence: 2Al + 2NaOH + 6H2O -> 2NaAl(OH)4 + 3H2; Zn + 2NaOH + 2H2O -> Na2Zn(OH)4 + H2. Industry confined-space practice (AS 2865 / OSHA 1910.146 atmospheric testing order: O2, flammables, toxics).

findings.issue: The slaker working principle reverses the 'drowning' term: 'too hot (boiling) drowns the particles'. Drowning is caused by too much water, which keeps the slaking temperature too low and gives coarse, unreactive hydrate. Too little water makes the slaker overheat ('burning'), which also lowers reactivity and can cause steam eruptions. An operator trained on the draft would correct the water ratio in the wrong direction.
findings.correction: 'Too much water (low slaking temperature) DROWNS the lime and gives coarse, low-surface-area hydrate. Too little water lets the slaker overheat and BURN the lime, also lowering reactivity and risking steam/slurry eruptions. Control the water:lime ratio to hold about 75-85 degC (as the supplier specifies).'
findings.evidence: Lime supplier slaking guidance (Carmeuse/Lhoist/National Lime Association bulletins) uses 'drowning' for excess water and low temperature and 'burning' for insufficient water.

findings.issue: Under mooring hazards the draft lists 'Mooring line snap-back zones (painted marking)'. OCIMF MEG4 (2018) advises against painting snap-back zones because painted areas give a false sense of safety. The whole mooring area should be treated as a potential snap-back zone.
findings.correction: 'Treat the whole mooring area on the wharf and dolphins as a snap-back danger zone (OCIMF MEG4). Keep personnel out during line tensioning and let-go. Use QRH remote release, and limit access to essential line handlers positioned out of line-of-bight. Do not rely on painted zones.'
findings.evidence: OCIMF Mooring Equipment Guidelines 4th ed. (2018), snap-back guidance. Web verification blocked, so confirm the clause.

findings.issue: The spent-liquor route is defined twice and the two definitions conflict. A11 collects spent liquor in 11-TK-001 at 55-62 degC, heats it to 82-90 degC in the PHEs and sends it to evaporation/digestion. A18 takes spent liquor at 55-65 degC from A12/A13 directly into 18-TK-001/002. The evaporator feed temperature, heat balance and which tank operators control are therefore ambiguous. A20 also uses ~3,050 m3/h without reference to the A11 heating.
findings.correction: Use one route: A12/A13 -> 11-TK-001 (spent liquor tank) -> PHE cold side (heated to 82-90 degC) -> split: about 1,700 m3/h to the A18 evaporator feed tank (now at about 85 degC, which changes the A18 effect temperature profile and steam economy) and about 1,350 m3/h bypass to the 18-TK-021/022 blend. Either delete 18-TK-001/002 or redefine them as hot evaporator feed tanks, and update the A18 feed temperature to 82-90 degC.
findings.evidence: Internal consistency of A11, A18 and A20 streams.

findings.issue: The mill feed bins and weigh feeders are specified twice with different tags, counts, sizes and feed sizes. A03 has 3 bins of 1,200-1,800 t with -40 mm feed. A04 has 4 bins (3+1) of 500-800 t with -25 mm feed. The wet rates also differ (720 vs 711 t/h). Training material would describe two different systems.
findings.correction: Keep one owner (A04) with 4 bins (3 operating + 1 standby line) and one live capacity (about 600-800 t each). Set one crushed top size: -25 mm if single-stage ball mills, with secondary sizers in A03 set to -25 mm. Make A03 end at the shuttle conveyor.
findings.evidence: Internal consistency.

findings.issue: The blow-off to clarification interface is duplicated and the process order conflicts. A07 pumps blow-off slurry with 3+3 pumps 'to the dilution tank'. A08 pumps from 'the last flash tank' with 2+1 pumps to the sand cyclones first and only then to the settler feed (dilution) tank. Operators would not know which pumps exist or whether sand removal is upstream of dilution.
findings.correction: A single train: 07-BT blow-off tanks -> 07-PP blow-off pumps -> 08-CY sand cyclones -> 08-TK-001 settler feed/dilution tank. Delete 08-PP-001 (or make it the only set) and align pump counts and NPSH notes.
findings.evidence: Internal consistency.

findings.issue: 'About 2 % of its mass evaporates per stage' contradicts the draft's own stage vapour of 12-13 t/h per unit on about 1,400-1,500 t/h slurry, which is about 0.85-0.9 % per stage. Related point in A06: 'about 7-8 % of the liquor flashes' on a leak at 145 degC overstates it slightly. The true value is about 5-6 %, though the hazard message still holds.
findings.correction: A07: 'about 0.8-1 % of the slurry mass evaporates per stage (about 5-6 % over all stages to atmospheric)'. A06: 'about 5-6 % of the released liquor flashes instantly to steam, so a leak expands to a large scalding steam/caustic-mist cloud'.
findings.evidence: m_vap/m = cp x dT / hfg = 3.2 x 6 / 2,200 = 0.9 % per 6 K stage; 3.3 x 39 / 2,230 = 5.8 % from 145 to 106 degC.

findings.issue: The tip 'never stop flow through a tank with the agitator still running unless the descaling procedure is followed' points trainees at the wrong risk. Isolating flow while agitation continues is the normal way to take a tank offline and drain it. The real hazard is loss of agitation with solids present (sanding), plus opening bottom doors on a non-empty tank.
findings.correction: 'Take a tank out of series only via the launder bypass gates. Keep the agitator running until the tank has been pumped down below the lower impeller. Never stop agitation on a tank holding slurry, and never open bottom access doors until the tank is empty and washed.'
findings.evidence: Standard precipitator take-out sequence; the A12 draft's own sanding hazards.

findings.issue: Standby pump philosophy contradicts between areas. A11 warns that a standby left with open isolations and no flow scales solid. A18 specifies standby 'on auto-start with suction and discharge valves open'.
findings.correction: Plant-wide rule: auto-start standbys in Bayer liquor service keep suction open with a small warm-through/recirculation bleed (or are condensate-flushed and rotated weekly). This prevents gibbsite/salt crystallisation in a stagnant casing, and the trainee rule should state it once.
findings.evidence: Internal consistency; gibbsite and oxalate crystallise in stagnant cooled liquor.

findings.issue: The draft says carbon steel is acceptable for 50 % NaOH 'below about 50-60 degC (no PWHT)'. On the NACE SP0403 caustic soda service chart, the no-PWHT carbon steel limit for 50 % NaOH is about 46-50 degC. Above about 70-80 degC nickel alloy is needed. A17 correctly says <50 degC.
findings.correction: 'Carbon steel without PWHT for 50 % NaOH only below about 45-50 degC (NACE SP0403 Area A). Keep heating-coil and steam-trace surface temperatures from creating local hot spots above this limit, and use low-pressure steam or tempered-water tracing.'
findings.evidence: NACE SP0403 caustic soda service chart (Area A/B/C boundaries); A17 draft statement.

findings.issue: Radiological (NORM) and trace-metal exposure from residue dust is not mentioned. Bauxite residue concentrates Th/U-series radionuclides and V, As and Cr. This matters for dust-exposure training at the RSA, filter house and sand stockpile, and for residue reuse.
findings.correction: Add to the RSA, filter-press and sand hazards: 'Residue may contain elevated naturally occurring radioactive material (Th-232, U-238 series) and trace metals. Control alkaline dust (PM10), carry out radiological characterisation per the local radiation regulator/IAEA SRS-49 guidance, and assess before reuse.'
findings.evidence: IAI Bauxite Residue Management Guidance (2015) and IAEA NORM literature on bauxite residue.

missing.name: Wet hydrate storage (hydrate storage silos/shed or agitated hydrate slurry storage tanks) between product filtration and calcination
missing.why: A15 itself notes that during a single-calciner outage (~2-3 weeks/yr each with 2 x 3,500 t/d units) ~2,000-2,500 t/d of hydrate must be stored or production cut. No equipment for this is defined in A14 or A15. Typical capacity is ~7-15 days of one calciner's feed (~15,000-35,000 t hydrate).

missing.name: Plant liquor inventory / emergency liquor storage tanks (spent, strong and pregnant liquor) and slurry dump/hold-up tanks
missing.why: These are needed to take liquor out of the circuit during digestion-unit shutdowns, thickener and precipitator descaling, and evaporator outages, and to absorb water-balance swings in the monsoon. Without them the 8,300 h availability and descaling rotations described in A06-A13 cannot be operated.

missing.name: On-line liquor analysers (thermometric titration autoanalysers for A, C, S, plus density) at digestion exit, settler overflow/PL, spent liquor and strong liquor
missing.why: Charge control (A04), digestion A/C, dilution control (A08), fill-temperature/yield control (A11/A12) and blend caustic (A18) all rely on frequent A/C and C measurement. Only lab samples or a vague 'online analyser' are mentioned.

missing.name: Excess fine-seed / fines destruction circuit (fines dissolution tank heated with spent or strong liquor, or routing to digestion)
missing.why: A13 mentions sending excess fines 'to digestion or CIP' after a nucleation event but provides no equipment. Fines destruction is a key PSD-cycle control tool in two-stage (Australian-style) precipitation.

missing.name: DSP seed recycle (residue underflow or DSP slurry return to pre-desilication tank 1)
missing.why: A05 lists DSP seed as a key rate lever and 'optional' in the interfaces, but defines no pump, line or tag. Seeded desilication is what lets 8-10 h at ~100 degC reach 70-90% conversion with low heater scaling.

missing.name: Product hydrate slurry storage tanks (2 x ~8,000-10,000 m3 agitated) with reclaim pumps
missing.why: Gives 3-5 days of buffer at one-calciner rate. Two 3,500 t/d calciners need this for refractory outages and trips, because precipitation cannot be turned down fast.

missing.name: Refinery liquor/spill catchment (emergency) pond or tank and area spill recovery header
missing.why: Bayer refineries keep a lined process-spill pond, or large emergency tanks, to receive a full tank or thickener inventory after loss of containment or during descaling drain-downs. None of A04-A19 provides one; the bunds only hold 110% of the largest tank locally.

missing.name: Digestion steam/relief SIS and dedicated quench/vent stack on 06-TK-201
missing.why: The relief system needs an explicitly sized two-phase dump tank and vent silencer for the blocked-outlet and let-down-valve-failed-open cases of 3 units. The 8 m x 12 m tank has no stated basis.

missing.name: Liquor (caustic inventory) storage tanks
missing.why: These hold spent or strong liquor during evaporator descale or digestion outages. The draft has only 1.5-3 h tanks, so a train descale forces a refinery rate cut.

missing.name: Precipitation emergency/descaling scale handling (scale breaker or crusher and scale return to digestion)
missing.why: A12 states that gibbsite scale is recycled to digestion, but no equipment is listed for crushing it and returning it to the mills or digestion.

missing.name: Third auxiliary boiler (or uprated aux boilers)
missing.why: Needed for N-1 steam capacity of ≥440 t/h once the HRSGs are corrected to ~90-100 t/h each.

missing.name: Bulk explosives precursor store and MMU depot (AN prill/emulsion silos, wash bay, licensed separation)
missing.why: The draft lists a contractor MMU and a magazine but no bulk AN/emulsion storage. A drill-and-blast ore mine at about 3 Mbcm/yr needs a licensed bulk depot.

missing.name: Surface miners (Wirtgen 2200/2500SM class) as an optional selective-mining fleet
missing.why: Surface miners are standard at East Coast India bauxite mines with hard ore. They remove blasting near communities and forests and give selective mining at the clay floor. Include them as a modelled option or an alternative fleet.

missing.name: Mine control room / FMS dispatch office and fibre/radio network
missing.why: The FMS is central to blending in the process description, but no physical control room, comms tower or repeater infrastructure is listed.

missing.name: Overland idler/belt maintenance vehicles (idler change unit, belt-lifting trolley, inspection drone/robot) and route substations
missing.why: A 20 km conveyor needs dedicated maintenance plant. The 33/6.6 kV substations at each drive station are mentioned only inside 02-DS and should be tagged separately for the 3-D model.

missing.name: Emergency stockpile feed conveyor and radial luffing stacker
missing.why: The rail side-stacker cannot reach a 120 m wide, 250-350 kt emergency pile (see findings).

missing.name: Stockyard roof/portal shed (monsoon option) and stockyard mobile fleet wash bay
missing.why: Wet monsoon ore causes bin hang-ups and mill-feed moisture swings. The roof is a major visual element if adopted and is currently only noted as optional.

missing.name: Dehumidified, dried aeration and airslide air supply for product silos
missing.why: SGA is hygroscopic (MOI spec). Silo aeration blowers at 0.5-0.8 bar(g) are listed without air drying or chilling, which tropical sites need.

missing.name: Shiploading surge bin / feed hopper with flow-control gate ahead of the wharf conveyor
missing.why: It holds a steady 2,000 t/h during silo changeover and gate adjustments, and allows trade weighing at a constant rate.

missing.name: Port off-spec / contaminated alumina reject bin and return path
missing.why: Rain-wetted or contaminated alumina at the port (spillage, conveyor cleanup) needs segregation and return. There is an off-spec silo at the refinery only.

missing.name: Common-user liquid berth/jetty (17-WH-002) and multipurpose berth (17-WH-003) with spill-response equipment (booms, skimmers, workboat)
missing.why: Caustic, HFO and diesel tankers and lime vessels are said to use these berths, but the structures, fenders, mooring and marine spill response are not tagged.

missing.name: Jetty conveyor spill trays / enclosed gallery floor and port stormwater/alumina capture sumps
missing.why: This prevents alumina and caustic reaching the sea and is a licensing requirement at alumina export terminals.

missing.name: Mercury condensers/removal on digestion and evaporator NCG vents, with Hg monitoring
missing.why: Mercury released at low-temperature digestion collects in vents, condensate pots and condensate. It needs engineered capture and safe maintenance procedures, which are missing from every area.

missing.name: Central control room/DCS, safety instrumented system (SIS) and plant-wide fire and gas detection
missing.why: Many areas refer to CCR, SIS trips and gas detection, but no area defines the CCR, alarm management, SIS logic owner, or the F&G system (gas station, GT enclosures, LBF, fuel tanks, H2 during acid cleaning).

missing.name: Emergency response/medical centre with caustic-burn and eye-injury treatment, decontamination and emergency vehicles
missing.why: Caustic burns are the most common serious injury in refineries. Only showers are specified; there is no site-level first-aid/medical, ambulance or ERT facility at the refinery (the mine has one).

missing.name: Hydrate storage (wet hydrate shed/tanks) between hydrate filtration and calcination
missing.why: A15 notes that during a single-calciner outage about 2,000-2,500 t/d of hydrate must be stored, but no equipment is defined. Without it, precipitation must cut back during calciner refractory outages.

missing.name: Refinery laboratory (process and product QA)
missing.why: Every area depends on lab results (A/C, C, SiO2, oxalate, TOC, LOI, BET, PSD, condensate Na), but the laboratory is not defined. It needs sample-handling safety for hot caustic and radiation-source registers.

missing.name: Refinery stormwater and contaminated-water management (bunded-area drainage system, caustic-contaminated stormwater ponds, process-water recovery)
missing.why: Each area has local sumps, but the plant-wide system that keeps caustic-contaminated runoff from leaving site in monsoon storms is missing.

consistency: [process] SCOPE AND STATUS: This review covers the complete draft (A01-A20). Live web verification was again blocked (WebSearch HTTP 403), so all checks rest on stoichiometry, mass and heat balances and standard Bayer literature. Items marked 'verify' still need a sourced check.

[process] CONFIRMED (plant-wide): 8,300 h/yr gives ~241 t/h; digestion 143-150 degC at 4.5-6.5 barg; digestion liquor C 270-290 g/L, PL ~240-250, spent ~235-250, strong 300-320 g/L as Na2CO3; A/C PL 0.68-0.72 and spent 0.36-0.39; yield ~76-81 g/L (yield = C x dA/C is internally correct); calcination 950-1,050 degC in GSC-HV/CFB at 2.8-3.1 GJ/t; theoretical heat of calcination ~2.0 GJ/t (checked: ~+204 kJ/mol Al2O3).

[process] CONFIRMED: sodalite DSP soda loss ~0.69 t Na2O per t reactive SiO2 (~37 kg Na2O/t Al2O3 at 2%), and caustic make-up ~75 kg NaOH/t, are consistent between A05, A08, A17 and A19. A17 import (120-200 kt/yr) and A19 (~150 kt/yr) agree.
[process] CONFIRMED: A07 flash train (6 stages, ~6-7 K per stage, ~75-78 t/h vapour per unit, saturation pressures 2.95 to 1.13 bar(a)) closes against the A06 heater duties (~40-45 MW per unit).

[process] CONFIRMED: the evaporation duty of ~420 t/h (1.75 t/t) roughly closes the water balance. Net water into the liquor circuit is: CCD wash (~550) minus W6 underflow liquor (~265) = ~285; plus hydrate wash net (~145); bauxite moisture (71); direct steam (~50-70); lime slurry water (~55); seals and flushes (~30). That totals ~640 t/h, against ~230 t/h removed as flash condensate in A07, leaving ~410 t/h. This will rise if digestion steam injection increases or the A06 configuration changes to slurry live-steam injection.
[process] CONFIRMED: LOI 24-26% in the A01 ore spec agrees with 40% available Al2O3 as gibbsite (21.2% combined water) plus goethite and kaolinite water.

[process] Pre-desilication (98-102 degC, 8-10 h), PL cooling to a 72-78 degC agglomeration fill, interstage cooling to 56-60 degC, and GSC-HV parameters are realistic for low-temperature Australian-style practice.

[process] Knock-on changes needed after the findings: the residue basis (~265-290 t/h) must be used in the A06/A07 stream tables. Steam demand (A20) rises to ~1.85-2.0 t/t once the dissolution endotherm is included. Cooling water (A20) rises to ~13,000-16,000 m3/h. The spent-liquor routing between A11 and A18 must be decided before 3-D layout of those areas.

[process] Area-numbering gaps: A11, A13 and A14 reference 'A?' for evaporation and digestion; these should be A18 and A06. A07/A08 both own 'process condensate tanks' (07-TK-001 vs 18-TK-012): define one owner.
[process] Seed-repulp practice (coarse seed repulped in a PL side-stream) is acceptable, but the repulp tanks then operate as small precipitators and will scale; this should be noted in A13.

[mechanical] Live web verification was not possible: WebSearch returned HTTP 403 (feature not enabled for the organisation). All corrections rest on standard engineering calculations (ASME VIII UG-20/27, API 650 5.6.3.2, API 521, Bond ball size, HRSG and cooling-water heat balances) and published practice from domain knowledge. Items marked 'verify' in the draft are still unverified.
[mechanical] Bauxite factor and dry feed: A01/A03 use 2.7 (650 t/h), A04-A07 and A20 use 2.65 (640 t/h), A08-A10 use 2.5-2.6 (600-630 t/h). Adopt 2.65 everywhere.
[mechanical] Residue: A06 gives 400-430 t/h, A08/A09 265 t/h, A20 280-300 t/h. Adopt ~285 t/h normal and ~310 t/h design.
[mechanical] Mill feed bins are specified in both A03 (3 bins, -40 mm) and A04 (4 bins, -25 mm). Assign them to A04 with -25 mm feed.
[mechanical] Blow-off pumping is defined in both A07 (07-PP to the dilution tank) and A08 (08-PP-001 to the sand cyclones). Keep one pumping step; cyclones go upstream of the dilution tank.

[mechanical] Cooling water: A20 gives 10,000 m3/h and 30-40 MW interstage; A12 gives 45-70 MW and 5,000-7,000 m3/h; A18 needs 5,000 m3/h; A11 trim adds up to 1,500 m3/h. Resize the tower to ~14,000-15,000 m3/h.

[mechanical] A5/A6 interface: A05 has 2 strings (~415 m3/h each) feeding 3 digestion units (~287 m3/h each). A distribution header or tank and the charge-pump suction arrangement need to be shown explicitly.
[mechanical] Refinery-to-port: A16/A17 assume an ~8 km overland conveyor, while the A20 layout assumes 30-60 km of rail. Pick one.
[mechanical] PL temperature: A10 filtrate is 95-102 degC but A11 feed is 100-106 degC. Align to 98-104 degC.
[mechanical] Lime: A17 imports 30-80 kt/yr but A20 consumes ~89 kt/yr quicklime. Align the import range to ~60-100 kt/yr.
[mechanical] Steam: A06 live steam (135-165 t/h) + A05 (25-40) + A18 (100) + A19 (20-30) + others ≈ 410 t/h is internally consistent. The steam generation capacity in A20 is not (see finding).
[mechanical] The A04 mill liquor (600-720 m3/h) + A06 liquor heaters (2,100-2,200) match the A18 blend output (2,750-2,900 m3/h). This is consistent.

[mining_logistics] Scope note: the relayed user request was only 'what is the current status?'. This output is the SME review step the workflow assigned. Status: all six domains have drafted A01-A20, and none of them, nor this review, could run live web verification (WebSearch returned HTTP 403 again in this run). Only Wikipedia 'Worsley Alumina' could be fetched, and it confirms ~50 km mine conveyor and 55 km to Bunbury.

[mining_logistics] The bauxite factor is still not one number: A01-A03 use 2.7 (650 t/h dry / 720 t/h wet), A04-A07 and A20 use 2.65 (640 / 711 t/h), and A08-A10 use 2.5-2.6 (600-630 t/h). Adopt one value (recommend 2.65-2.7) and carry it through mine tonnage, stockyard, mill feed and residue.

[mining_logistics] The deposit model and ore grade disagree: the mine text and fleet describe Darling Range (thin, friable, free-dig, 60-110 ha/yr), but the grade basis is India East Coast (45-48% total Al2O3, ~40% available). Mining method, pit depth, drill fleet, strip ratio and disturbance area must follow the East Coast choice, or the grade must change.
[mining_logistics] Mine ROM (6.2-6.4 Mt wet) does not equal refinery bauxite consumption (~5.9-6.0 Mt wet); see the dilution double-count finding.
[mining_logistics] A03/A04 duplicate the mill feed bins and weigh feeders (03-BN/WF vs 04-BN/WF), with 3 vs 4 bins, 1,200-1,800 t vs 500-800 t per bin, and -40 mm vs -25 mm feed size.
[mining_logistics] Refinery-to-port transport (8 km conveyor in A16/A17 vs 30-60 km rail in A20) and caustic receipt (pipeline in A17 vs rail/road bays in A19) need one decision before 3-D modelling.
[mining_logistics] The overland 'regenerative' claim in A02 is inconsistent with its own power figures; the conveyor is net motoring at a 0.75% average decline.
[mining_logistics] The primary sizer, overland and stockyard (1,800 t/h for 4,300-4,900 h) and the truck fleet (6,000 h/yr) use different mine operating hours; state one mine roster.
[mining_logistics] Lime demand differs: A17 says 30-80 kt/yr CaO, A20 says ~89 kt/yr quicklime (~40 kg CaO/t). Caustic agrees at ~150 kt/yr NaOH (A17/A19).

[mining_logistics] Monsoon basis: refinery strategic stock is 15-20 days, and the effective emergency reclaim rate is below mill demand. Indian East Coast practice often builds 30-45+ days of pre-monsoon stock at the mine or refinery; confirm against the chosen climate.

[mining_logistics] Fuel basis affects import logistics: if the generic plant follows Indian practice (coal-fired CFBC), the port and site need coal import, unloading and stockyard equipment, none of which is in A17 or A20. If natural gas, A17 fuel oil is backup only.

[hse_training] WebSearch/WebFetch were blocked (HTTP 403) in this review as well, so findings rest on standards and domain knowledge. The mercury, OCIMF MEG4 and NACE SP0403 references should be confirmed by SME/document check.
[hse_training] Bauxite factor is inconsistent: A01-A03 use 2.7, A04-A07 and A20 use 2.65, and A08-A10 use 2.5-2.6 (5.0-5.2 Mt/yr). Adopt 2.65 t/t (about 640 t/h dry) throughout.
[hse_training] Caustic (C) of first-washer overflow: A08 says 80-140 g/L, A19/A20 say 100-170 g/L. Align.

[hse_training] Safety shower spacing is consistent (10 s per ANSI Z358.1, about 15-17 m). Keep a plant-wide statement of minimum 15 min tempered flushing, with eye exposures to alkali flushed much longer (up to 60 min) and urgent medical review.
[hse_training] PWHT philosophy for caustic service is applied inconsistently between atmospheric tanks (A04/A05/A11/A18). It needs one owner materials philosophy based on the NACE SP0403 chart.

[hse_training] Radiation sources (PGNAA Cf-252 in A03, radiometric density/level gauges in A04, A06, A07, A08 and A12) need one plant radiation-safety management plan and source register for trainees.
